channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Iran Asks UN to Condemn US Naval Blockade of Its Ports
item.description: Iran's UN representative has urged the UN Security Council to condemn and reject the US naval blockade of Iranian ports in the Strait of Hormuz and the Persian Gulf. In a letter, Iran requested the US cease military aggression and warned of exercising self-defense rights.

item.title: Bazar-Korgon District Requires Nearly 2 Billion Som for Development
item.description: The Bazar-Korgon district requires nearly 2 billion som for its development. President Sadyr Japarov reviewed the socio-economic development of the district in the Jalal-Abad region. Industrial production volume increased significantly, and 56 facilities were built between 2021 and 2026. Further infrastructure projects, including wastewater treatment plants and roads, are planned.

item.title: Sadyr Japarov Proposes Developing Walnut Processing in Bazar-Korgon
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has proposed developing walnut processing in Kyrgyzstan's Bazar-Korgon district and promoting the national brand 'Natural Kyrgyz Walnut'. He highlighted the region's significant natural potential due to its walnut forests. The initiative aims to shift from exporting raw materials to producing finished products like walnut oil, paste, and flour, thereby increasing added value.

item.title: All 58 Students Hospitalized for Intestinal Infection in Almaty Discharged
item.description: All 58 students from the Republican Physics and Mathematics School (RFMS) in Almaty who were hospitalized due to an intestinal infection have been discharged. The students are recovering after receiving medical treatment for the illness.

item.title: Mysterious Death of 62-Year-Old Man Reported in Istaravshan
item.description: A 62-year-old man has died under mysterious circumstances in Istaravshan, with stab wounds found on his body. His wife has been hospitalized following the incident, which occurred on the night of October 10th in the village of Bobotagho.

item.title: Lawyers for Bokaev Denied Recusal of Judge Again
item.description: The court denied the defense's request to recuse Judge Zhanat Abenova in the case of civil activist Sanzhar Bokaev. Lawyers cited concerns over the defendants' seating arrangement and the alleged forced appointment of a new lawyer for Ulan Nusipkozha.

item.title: Chuy Regional Maternity Hospital Plans December Relocation Amid Renovation
item.description: The Chuy Regional Maternity Hospital is preparing to move to a renovated building, with the relocation planned before December 1, 2026. The Ministry of Health reports that building repairs are nearly complete, with only linoleum installation remaining. Gas line connection to the boiler room is the final engineering task. The move aims to provide a more comfortable and safe environment for mothers and newborns.

item.title: Kazakhmys Pursues New Parks, Sports Facilities, and University in Ulytau Region
item.description: Kazakhmys Corporation chairman Ruslan Oskenali reviewed social and infrastructure projects in Ulytau region on October 21. Key areas include public spaces, sports, and education. Projects include the Ken Gir reservoir embankment, the Namys Academy sports complex with dormitories, and the reconstruction of Zhas Tar park, aiming for completion in Q4 2026. The company is funding these initiatives.

item.title: New City of Qarshi for 500,000 Residents to Be Built in Qashqadaryo Region
item.description: Uzbekistan plans to build a new city, New Qarshi, covering 5,000 hectares in the Qashqadaryo region to accommodate a population of 500,000. President Shavkat Mirziyoyev announced the plan, citing growing housing demand due to population increase.

item.title: Ukraine Awaits US Response on Starlink Restrictions, Lawmakers Demand Investigation
item.description: Ukraine has not yet received a response from the Pentagon or SpaceX regarding restrictions on its military's use of satellite internet. The Ukrainian interim charge d'affaires in Washington confirmed this, stating that Kyiv has received no answers. Meanwhile, bipartisan support is growing in Congress for an investigation into the matter.

item.title: Taliban Intelligence Member Killed in Takhar, Freedom Front Claims
item.description: The Afghanistan Freedom Front announced that a member of the Taliban's intelligence agency was killed in the province of Takhar. Further details regarding the incident were not immediately available. The claim was made by the opposition group, which has been active in opposing the Taliban regime.

item.title: Court keeps activist Sanzhar Bokeyev and associate in detention
item.description: A court in Almaty has decided to keep activist Sanzhar Bokeyev and Madiyar Kalmenov in detention, rejecting a request to change their pre-trial restrictive measures. Bokeyev's videographer, Ulan Nussipkozha, was moved to house arrest due to health reasons. Bokeyev has been in custody since March, facing charges including fraud and spreading false information. Supporters claim the case has political undertones.

item.title: US Diplomats Ordered to Leave Saudi Arabia Amidst Escalating Attacks
item.description: US diplomats not involved in emergency services have been ordered to leave Saudi Arabia. This decision comes amid escalating attacks by Houthi rebels. The evacuation aims to ensure the safety of personnel and their families in the region.

item.title: Kazakhstan Mine Found Discharging Polluted Water into River After Resident Complaints
item.description: Environmentalists in Kazakhstan's East Kazakhstan region discovered violations at the Dengbo Success Minerals LTD mine after complaints from residents. The mine was found to be discharging untreated шахтные воды (mine water) into the Berezovka River during commissioning works. The company faced administrative penalties and its case was sent to court.

item.title: Astana Prosecutor's Office declares journalist's travel ban illegal
item.description: The Astana Prosecutor's Office has declared the travel ban imposed on journalist Lukpan Akhmedyarov illegal. Akhmedyarov, author of the YouTube channel 'Simply Journalism,' stated that the ban was applied unlawfully as he is a witness with the right to defense, not a suspect. The prosecutor's office has requested the investigator to lift the ban.

item.title: Maternal mortality rate in Kyrgyzstan decreased by 34.4% in first nine months of 2026
item.description: Maternal mortality in Kyrgyzstan has decreased by 34.4% in the first nine months of 2026, according to the Ministry of Health. The ministry reported 23 maternal deaths during this period. The maternal mortality rate was 22.1 per 100,000 live births, a significant decrease from the previous year. Family planning services and support for pregnant women remain priorities.

item.title: Kazakhstan Banks Must Assess Borrowers' Environmental Risks: Are They Ready?
item.description: Banks in Kazakhstan will be required to assess the environmental risks of their borrowers. The article questions their preparedness for this new regulatory requirement and explores the implications for the financial sector.

item.title: Economist: Kazakhstan's Economy Stuck, Needs Technological Shift to Combat Inequality
item.description: Economist Rakhymbek Abdrakhmanov argues Kazakhstan's economy relies too heavily on raw material rent, hindering the development of a stable middle class and exacerbating inequality. He proposes a shift towards technological production and improved governance to create a sustainable future.

item.title: Kazakhstan Submits Bid to Host Futsal EURO 2030 Finals
item.description: Kazakhstan is among seven nations bidding to host the Futsal EURO 2030 finals. Croatia, Finland, France, Georgia, Poland, and Spain are also contenders. UEFA confirmed a record number of applications, indicating growing popularity of futsal. The host nation will be decided in September 2027.

item.title: Kazakhstan Border Guards Seize 620 Saiga Horns Destined for China
item.description: Kazakh border guards have intercepted an attempt to illegally smuggle 620 saiga antelope horns into China. The seized horns have an estimated black market value of approximately 180 million tenge. A criminal investigation has been launched into the incident, which occurred at the Khorgos border cooperation center.

item.title: Kazakhstan Sees Rising Savings and Debt Amidst Economic Shifts
item.description: Kazakhstan citizens are increasingly saving money, but their debt burden is also growing. AERC expert Yerassyl Serikbay explains that while affluent individuals contribute to savings, lower-income populations are relying on loans to offset declining real incomes. The National Bank's report indicates a decrease in real incomes throughout 2025, weakening purchasing power despite nominal gains.

item.title: US Congresswoman Accuses Israel of Genocide Against Palestinians
item.description: US Congresswoman Delia Ramirez has accused Israel of committing genocide against Palestinians, alleging it is funded by the United States. She stated on X that Israel continues to kill children and families in Gaza via airstrikes, while half a million Palestinians face starvation. Ramirez urged an end to the violence and called for support of the 'Block the Bombs' legislation.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Russia Mark 34 Years of Diplomatic Ties, Affirming Cooperation
item.description: Kazakhstan and Russia are celebrating the 34th anniversary of establishing diplomatic relations. Embassies exchanged congratulations, highlighting the development of their strategic partnership and alliance. Diplomatic ties were established on October 22, 1992. Both nations emphasized the growth of cooperation across all sectors and the importance of high-level meetings, noting a bilateral trade turnover of $27.4 billion in 2025.

item.title: Investors Target Kazakhstan for Renewable Energy and Raw Material Processing
item.description: International investors view Kazakhstan as a promising hub for investments in renewable energy, industry, and deep raw material processing. Representatives from foreign companies at the IX Kazakhstan Global Investment Roundtable (KGIR 2026) in Shymkent highlighted this potential. Masdar plans further renewable energy projects, while Tamasuk Holding emphasized the need to transition from memorandums to concrete, profitable projects.

item.title: Qashqadaryo plans to attract 6 million tourists annually, 2.5 million visited this year
item.description: Qashqadaryo region aims to attract 6 million tourists per year, with 2.5 million visitors already recorded since the beginning of the year. The President has ordered the launch of new projects in six villages to enhance the region's tourism potential.

item.title: Kazakhstan stops illegal export of gold-containing ore worth 1.5 billion tenge
item.description: Kazakhstan's Financial Monitoring Agency has halted the illegal export of 2,600 tons of gold-containing ore, valued at 1.5 billion tenge. The ore was falsely declared as copper ore and concentrates to conceal its actual composition. Over a thousand tons of similar raw material were found at warehouses.

item.title: Italy Trucker Strike Disrupts Food and Fuel Deliveries
item.description: A multi-day strike by truck drivers in southern Italy has caused disruptions in the delivery of goods. Drivers are protesting high fuel prices. While protests have eased in Calabria and Sicily, supply chain issues persist, leading to empty shelves and business closures.

item.title: Driver Dies After Construction Vehicle Overturns in Tajikistan
item.description: A driver operating a road construction machine in Tajikistan's Vose district died on October 19, 2026, after losing control of the vehicle. The machine overturned into a 17-meter-deep ravine. The 29-year-old driver sustained injuries and passed away en route to the hospital. Investigations into the cause are ongoing.

item.title: UNAMA Security Official in Bamyan Unharmed After Armed Attack
item.description: The security official for the UN Assistance Mission in Afghanistan (UNAMA) in Bamyan province, Karim Karimi, survived an armed attack on Wednesday. His vehicle came under gunfire in the provincial capital, but he was unharmed. This incident follows a joint warning from resistance groups about potential attacks on international organizations.

item.title: Kazakhstan Border Guards Seize 620 Saiga Horns Destined for China
item.description: Kazakhstan's National Security Committee reported that border guards at the "Khorgos" international border cooperation center intercepted an attempt to illegally export 620 saiga horns to China on October 20. The black market value of the horns is estimated at around 180 million tenge. The case materials have been transferred to the relevant authorities.

item.title: Kazakhstan's Internet Shutdown Legality Questioned Amid Constitutional Court Rulings
item.description: The legality of internet shutdowns, experienced by Kazakhstan in January 2022, was discussed at the Qazaqstan IGF-2026 forum. A lawsuit challenging the shutdown faced a legal deadlock, as operators cited government orders. Laws on emergency situations and communications allow national security bodies to disconnect the internet without a court order. The Constitutional Court's role in these rulings is under scrutiny.

item.title: Half of Uzbekistan's Irrigated Land is Salinized, Study Finds Water Use Inefficient
item.description: A study reveals that half of Uzbekistan's irrigated land is affected by salinization, and the country struggles with efficient water use. Approximately 37% of water is lost during canal irrigation. The report highlights the ongoing challenge of effectively managing water resources for agricultural purposes in the nation.

item.title: Kazakhstan Sees Decline in Youth Not in Education, Employment, or Training
item.description: The proportion of young people in Kazakhstan categorized as NEET (Not in Education, Employment, or Training) is decreasing. Official statistics show a drop from 7.1% in 2020 to a projected 6% by 2025 and 5.7% by mid-2026. The number of unemployed and out-of-school youth aged 15-34 has also fallen significantly.

item.title: Uzbekistan Adopts New Latin-Based Alphabet with 28 Letters
item.description: Uzbekistan has enacted a new law to refine its Latin-based alphabet, effective six months after publication. The updated alphabet will feature 28 letters and one apostrophe, replacing three digraphs with single characters like 'ö' for 'oʻ' and 'ğ' for 'gʻ'. This change aligns with the principle of 'one sound, one letter' and international Turkic alphabets.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Transfer All Mosques to Spiritual Administration of Muslims
item.description: All active mosques in Kyrgyzstan will be transferred to the balance of the Spiritual Administration of Muslims of Kyrgyzstan. This process is linked to a government review of mosque documentation. The Spiritual Administration reports 4470 mosques nationwide, many built with private funds and lacking complete paperwork. The transfer aims to align with the law on religious freedom, requiring religious objects to be under the central governing body's balance. The process is expected to conclude by February 1, 2027.

item.title: Dushanbe Hosts International Forum "IP Eurasia / IP Tajikistan-2026"
item.description: An international forum titled "IP Eurasia / IP Tajikistan-2026" was held in Dushanbe on October 21, 2026, initiated by the Ministry of Economic Development and Trade of Tajikistan. The event gathered participants from the Eurasian Patent Office, foreign patent offices, and relevant Tajik ministries. Discussions focused on the importance of intellectual property for economic development, entrepreneurship, and product competitiveness, as well as technology transfer and commercialization of research.

item.title: Taliban Report Over 1,000 People Forcibly Returned to Afghanistan
item.description: The Taliban announced that 1,020 people, comprising 234 families, have been forcibly returned to Afghanistan. Deputy spokesperson Hamdullah Fitrat stated that individuals entered through Torkham in Nangarhar, the Silk Road crossing in Nimroz, Spin Boldak in Kandahar, and Islam Qala in Herat province.

item.title: Kazakhstan Reports Return of Citizens from Ukraine War Zone
item.description: Lawyer Meirman Shekeev announced that 13 Kazakh citizens are being prepared for release from the conflict zone in Ukraine, with at least one, 20-year-old Ainabek Keldibek, having returned home. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs is taking necessary measures for citizens who were deceived into signing documents and sent to fight. Dozens of parents protested at the ministry in Astana.

item.title: WHO Reports Over 30 Malnourished Children Treated Monthly in Herat
item.description: A malnutrition treatment center in Herat province's Guzara district, supported by the WHO and EU funding, treats over 30 severely malnourished children monthly. The UN warns of increasing acute malnutrition in Afghanistan, projecting over four million children needing treatment by 2027, with critical levels expanding to 10 provinces.

item.title: Governments take websites offline amid global alert over critical cyber flaws
item.description: Governments and organizations worldwide are taking websites offline due to critical vulnerabilities in widely used web software. Patches have been released, urging immediate updates or service shutdowns to prevent malicious code execution.
